operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still must double-quote ("id", "genre_name") and compare case-insensitively.
region_sales has NO primary key (pk=[]): sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
region_sales is the only table with a REAL column (num_sales) and no PK; it is the largest (65320 rows) but well under max_rows_per_table.
All FKs resolve to existing parents with unique PKs (genre.id, game.id, publisher.id, platform.id, game_publisher.id, game_platform.id); no dangling/self FKs.
FK columns are declared nullable (notnull=0) but null_rate=0.0 everywhere; TS may still emit NULLs for empty parents.
release_year is INTEGER storing years 1981..2011 (39 distinct) -> dispatches to Number fuzzer, NOT Date; TS will produce arbitrary ints, not plausible years.
game_publisher.game_id distinct=11360 < rows=11732: many-to-one to game (a game can have several publishers); FK draw with replacement is fine.
game_platform.game_publisher_id distinct=11732 = game_publisher rows: effectively 1:1-ish but not declared unique.
region has only 4 rows; region_sales.region_id FK draws from 4 values -> heavy duplication, fine.
genre (12), platform (31), region (4) are tiny parents; TS level-0 sizes 1+30u may exceed them, but FK draw is with replacement so no error.
All storage classes match declared types (integer/real/text); no text-stored dates, no type-affinity contradictions.
DDL uses 'default NULL' and lowercase 'foreign key'/'primary key'; line-based unique/check scan finds no unique/check lines (only PKs).
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all *_id and release_year: uniform ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale from type args; INTEGER -> scale 0 -> roughly [-1,1] then perturbed +-1/+-2), so ids are tiny and collide heavily.
String fuzzer on *_name columns: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20, plus 5 sampled originals and pool literals; contaminate adds junk -> implausible names (FN source for name filters).
release_year via Number: values like -1,0,1,2 instead of 1981..2011 -> queries filtering year ranges return empty/odd -> FN.
num_sales via Number(REAL): scale 0 -> ints in [-1,1] perturbed, not the 0.01..3.5 real distribution -> sales thresholds (e.g. >1) behave wrongly -> FN/FP.
PK ids drawn from Number then deduped by sample_fresh_primary_keys: after dedup, id space collapses to small ints; joins still work but cardinalities shrink.

FK columns drawn from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> referential integrity holds, but parent tables tiny (region=4) so region_sales rows collapse onto few region_ids -> missing ties/duplicates -> FP on DISTINCT/COUNT.
region_sales has no PK and no unique cols: no dedup at all -> duplicate (region_id,game_platform_id) rows possible -> FP for queries assuming uniqueness.
Empty-parent case: if a parent table's PK dedup leaves 0 rows (unlikely here) child FK -> NULLs; not expected on this DB.
String pool literals from train SQL (e.g. 'Action','Wii','North America') get mixed with random strings -> some plausible, some junk -> mixed FN/FP.
Number list-range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) means even with pool literals like 2007, fresh draws dominate -> release_year rarely plausible.
Bool/Bit/Date/Time fuzzers unused (no such declared types) -> no date-template behaviour to worry about.
Composite/self FKs absent -> process_order is a clean 6-level DAG (genre,platform,publisher,region -> game -> game_publisher -> game_platform -> region_sales).
